'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[Twelve-Day War]] 
***[[2025 Iran–European nuclear talks]]
****[[Iran]]ian [[Minister of Foreign Affairs (Iran)|foreign minister]] [[Abbas Araghchi]] meets with the [[foreign minister]]s of the [[United Kingdom]], [[Germany]], [[France]] and [[European Union]] in [[Geneva]] for talks about its [[Nuclear program of Iran|nuclear program]]. [https://apnews.com/article/iran-nuclear-geneva-talks-europe-israel-0c9b3dff338f279c85d94885cb1b51b8 (AP)] 
***Hundreds of thousands of people protest against Israel on the streets of [[Tehran]] after [[Salah|weekly prayers]], chanting slogans in support of Iranian leaders. Protests also took place in [[Tabriz]] in northwestern Iran and [[Shiraz]] in the south. [https://aje.io/asdg2r?update=3788002 (Al Jazeera)]
***[[Saudi Arabia]]'s Nuclear and Radiological Regulatory Commission says military strikes on civilian nuclear facilities violate [[international law]] in response to Israeli strikes on Iranian nuclear facilities. [https://aje.io/asdg2r?update=3787994 (Al Jazeera)]
**[[Gaza war]]
***[[Rafah aid distribution killings]]
****[[Israel Defense Forces|Israeli]] gunfire and airstrikes kill at least 82 [[Palestinians]] across the [[Gaza Strip]], including 34 people seeking [[Humanitarian aid during the Gaza war|aid assistance]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/6/20/at-least-35-killed-in-new-israeli-attack-on-gaza-aid-seekers (Al Jazeera)]
***The [[United Nation]]s relists Israel on its blacklist of countries committing [[abuse]]s against children in [[armed conflict]] in its annual Children in Armed Conflict report. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/6/20/israel-again-included-in-un-blacklist-for-grave-violations-against-children (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Odesa strikes (2022–present)|Odesa strikes]]
***[[Russian Armed Forces|Russian forces]] launch a large-scale [[drone warfare|drone]] strike at [[Odesa]], [[Ukraine]], damaging buildings and public facilities, with one person killed and another 14 injured. [https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2025/06/20/7517947/ (''Ukrainska Pravda'')] 

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Nine people are killed after a head-on collision between a truck and a car in [[West Bengal]], [[India]]. [https://www.ndtv.com/cities/9-killed-in-car-truck-collision-in-west-bengal-8714578 (NDTV)]
*Four people are missing after a [[MBB/Kawasaki BK 117|Kawasaki]] [[air medical services|medical helicopter]] on a rescue operation crashes north of [[Baie-Johan-Beetz]] near [[Natashquan]] on the [[Côte-Nord]] in [[Quebec]], [[Canada]]. The pilot is found and taken to hospital. [https://ici.radio-canada.ca/nouvelle/2174324/ecrasement-helicoptere-cote-nord-quatre-personnes-disparus-natashqua (CBC)]

'''International relations'''
*[[France–Niger relations]]
**The [[Government of Niger|Nigerien government]] announces it will [[nationalization|nationalize]] the controlling share of the [[SOMAIR]] mining company that previously belonged to [[France|French]] [[multinational corporation|multinational]] [[nuclear fuel cycle]] corporation [[Orano]], which is in turn controlled by the [[French government]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/niger-to-nationalize-french-share-in-uranium-company-somair/a-72979089 (DW)] [https://apnews.com/article/niger-uranium-somair-orano-sahel-4a3a9490d9c4f89edd3906a98ba2f79a (AP)]
*[[Singapore–Vietnam relations]]
**The governments of [[Singapore]] and [[Vietnam]] sign a [[memorandum]] to exchange 300 to 1,000 [[skilled worker]]s between the countries annually. [https://e.vnexpress.net/news/news/education/vietnam-singapore-to-exchange-1-000-talented-workers-each-year-under-new-program-4903941.html (''VnExpress'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Detention of Mahmoud Khalil]]
**[[Columbia University]] student activist Mahmoud Khalil is released from prison, after being in custody for three months. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/mahmoud-khalil-ordered-released-federal-judge-rcna214163 (NBC News)]
*The [[United Kingdom parliament]] votes to approve a [[Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill|bill]] allowing [[terminal illness|terminally ill]] adults to voluntarily end their lives, moving towards legalizing [[assisted suicide]] in [[England]] and [[Wales]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/uk-parliament-backs-assisted-dying-bill-in-historic-vote/a-72988943 (DW)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/live/cg4ry0pge4kt (BBC News)]
